newsitem.title: USA: BASKETBALL-UNIVERSITY OF GEORGIA TABS ASSISTANT JIRSA AS COACH.
newsitem.headline: BASKETBALL-UNIVERSITY OF GEORGIA TABS ASSISTANT JIRSA AS COACH.

text.p: The University of Georgia turned to one of its own to take over the men's basketball team, promoting assistant Ron Jirsa to head coach on Monday.
Jirsa takes over from Tubby Smith, who left Georgia last Monday to replace new Boston Celtics chief Rick Pitino as coach of Kentucky.
Georgia Athletic Director Vince Dooley said Jirsa's total package would be worth about $300,000 per year.
"He's ready," Dooley added. "There's no question he's hungry, and he is certainly excited about this opportunity."
The 37-year-old Jirsa has been Smith's right-hand man through the years since meeting him at Virginia Commonwealth, where the two were assistant coaches for the 1984-85 season.

In 1991, Smith became head coach at Tulsa and asked Jirsa to join him. He was an assistant for two seasons and was associate head coach in 1994 and 1995 before both came over to Georgia prior to the 1995-96 season.
Jirsa was chief recruiting coach for Smith at Georgia and helped Smith create a team that went 24-9 last season despite losing its entire starting lineup from 1996's Sweet 16 team.
The entire Bulldogs team is expected to return. The only possible defection is Smith's son, G.G. Smith, who has not announced whether he will transfer and join his father at Kentucky.
